Hi Sophie — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Summary of ask:
- Orion wants to ensure all PII inference requests for US retail customers remain within US data centers and are not processed in EU/APAC.
- You also asked about cross-region failover behavior, backups, and logging/audit controls for debug and compliance.

Open questions for the team (could you confirm these when you have a moment):
1) Which data elements you consider PII for the use case (names, email, account numbers, SSN, device IDs?) — we want to map level-of-scrubbing vs. retention.
2) Retention windows for prompts/results and for audit logs (e.g., 30 / 90 / 365 days).
3) Any requirement for customer-managed keys (KMS) for backup encryption or in-transit crypto beyond our defaults.

What I promised on the call:
- Aditya will send a short technical note on how Redwood handles region pinning and what triggers cross-region failover.
- We'll share a one-page summary of backup/replication behavior and options for KMS.
- Propose a 30-minute technical deep dive next week with your infra team to walk runbooks.

I've attached our region-pinning overview (redwood-region-pinning-v1.pdf) and an editable spreadsheet to capture the specific data fields (orion-data-requirements.xlsx).

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few answers and clarifications from our side: 

PII scope:
- Primary: names, email addresses, account numbers, partial SSN (last 4) — these must remain in-region (US) for retail workloads.
- Secondary: device IDs and session metadata — acceptable to process outside US if pseudonymized, but prefer US where possible.

Retention:
- Prompts/results: 90 days for troubleshooting, longer only by explicit opt-in.
- Audit logs: 365 days (regulatory retention requirement).

Encryption/KMS:
- We would prefer Customer-Managed Keys for backups and long-term storage; in-transit TLS is standard.

Failover:
- We need an architecture that preserves the in-region processing guarantee for normal ops. For disaster/failover, we need a documented playbook that explains when cross-region processing would be used and the minimum data set allowed to fail over.

Agree on the 30-min deep dive. Raj and I are available next Tue/Wed morning EST. Could you include your infra lead?

Thanks,

Hi Sophie — looping in a few technical details to address the questions you raised. Below is an overview of how Redwood supports the requirements you described and configuration options.

1) Region pinning and request routing
- Per-tenant region pinning: we can configure a tenant policy that routes inference traffic for specific routes to a primary region (eg. us-west-2) and blocks routing to non-approved regions.
- Model variants: for high-availability we support pinned model variants (same model weights deployed to multiple regions). Failover is policy-controlled — by default we avoid cross-region failover for pinned routes unless a customer enables emergency cross-region failover.

2) Cross-region failover behavior
- Trigger conditions: capacity exhaustion, region outage, or manual failover action.
- Failover policy types: 
  a) Strict (no cross-region processing) — requests will queue / return 503 if primary region unavailable.
  b) Emergency (allow minimal processing in secondary region) — only non-PII or pseudonymized payloads, or explicit opt-in for specific routes.
- Audit trail: every failover event records a detailed audit entry (timestamp, reason, affected routes, tokens processed) retained per your audit retention policy.

3) Backups and replication
- Model state & persistent metadata: replicated to configured regions asynchronously; backups are encrypted at rest.
- Customer-managed KMS: supported for long-term backups and snapshot exports.

4) Logging and retention controls
- Request logs (non-payload metadata) default retention 90 days configurable up to 2 years; full request/response payload logs are off by default and can be enabled with strict access controls.
- Access: audit logs are available via Console and can be exported to your SIEM (S3/GCS) with retention matching your policy.

Attached is a short runbook link and a one-page failover matrix. Happy to expand any of these sections in the deep dive.

—Aditya

2) Log export with customer KMS: supported — we can push audit and request logs to your S3 bucket with SSE-KMS using your key. We'll need an IAM role and a short perms list (I can share).
